top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock (Katori and Ye) rests on one clean mechanism, the magic-wavelength trap, and its 1e-18 performance has been reproduced and surpassed independently at several national laboratories. It now yields clues from nature: millimetre-scale gravitational redshift, bounds on drifting constants and dark-matter couplings. It is distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, the credit chain is short and was proposed identically by all eight members, and a citation naming the invention and the 1e-18 performance it enabled keeps the scope honest. The remaining weaknesses (invention rather than discovery, omitted contributors, second not yet redefined) do not outweigh a mature, confirmed achievement, so I prefer awarding it to no award.
